leading_positions.synthesis: Seven of eight round-1 files name B012 (optical lattice clocks, Katori and Ye) as the sole prize part. All seven give the same core reasons: a single magic-wavelength idea, roughly 10^-18 fractional uncertainty, independent reproduction on several continents, and a two-name allocation. Danielsson and Johansson moved to B012 from other opening first choices (B028 and B005 respectively), and Pearce moved from B042. The seven citations are not identical in wording: some anchor on the magic-wavelength lattice and many-atom interrogation, others add geodesy and tests of fundamental constants, and Mehlig's mentions relativistic geodesy explicitly. Shared reservations (Wineland 2012 and comb 2005 overlap, other lattice-clock groups, the pending redefinition of the second) are carried in every file, but members differ on how much weight they carry. Eriksson ranked B012 eighth in the opening, now lists it as an alternative, and does not prefer it.

Eriksson alone prefers B030 (Kane, Mele, Molenkamp) as the sole prize part, as the most defensible common ground within condensed matter, with a concept (Z2 invariant, quantum spin Hall effect) and a decisive HgTe observation. He names B042 and B012 as alternatives. B030 appears as an alternative in the files of Johansson, Lindroth, Mehlig and Pearce, but none of them prefers it. Support is therefore broad but shallow, and the case is limited by the omission of Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang (BHZ) and of the three-dimensional topological-insulator work, and by the 2016 prize on topological phases of matter. Kroll explicitly would not put B030 in a preferred configuration this year, and Olsson ranked it sixth in her opening.

areas_of_agreement: No file prefers a configuration with more than one prize part; every preferred configuration is a single part (seven B012, one B030).

The magic-wavelength lattice is described by all seven B012 supporters as a distinct idea from frequency combs (2005) and single-ion control (2012), and several ask that the citation be worded around the lattice and many-atom interrogation so it does not re-award earlier work.
Katori and Ye is the only laureate configuration proposed for B012, and no member argues that a third name from the supplied list is missing.

B042 (twisted bilayer graphene) is widely regarded as a serious and original competitor: it appears as an alternative for Danielsson, Eriksson, Kroll, Lindroth, Johansson, Mehlig, Olsson and Pearce. Members who rank it below B012 do so on maturity and attribution, not on merit.

Several members (Danielsson, Eriksson, Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig, Olsson, Pearce) treat circuit QED (B005) as not ready for a preferred configuration this year, mainly because of timing after the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in superconducting circuits. Johansson, who ranked it first in the opening, discloses a conflict and no longer proposes it.
Members agree that opening-ballot support is not by itself evidence of merit, and several say so explicitly.
scientific_disputes: Eriksson holds that a conceptual advance that changed how a class of materials is understood (B030) should outrank a precision-measurement advance, and has not been persuaded otherwise. Mehlig names the same tension (conceptual discovery versus instrument achievement) as open; Olsson, Kroll and Pearce are comfortable treating the instrument as the achievement.

Whether the lattice clock is a new idea or an evolutionary refinement in the comb, single-ion and lattice sequence. Lindroth, Kroll, Olsson and Pearce say the lattice concept is distinct. Johansson notes that ion clocks reach comparable uncertainty and asks that the citation not rest on accuracy in general. Danielsson and Kroll ask for the overlap to be checked against the history.

Whether B042 has a stronger scientific footprint than B012. Pearce's own file concedes B042 has the larger recent footprint, while Johansson, Lindroth, Kroll, Mehlig and Olsson argue that the unresolved origin of the superconductivity and of other correlated states makes it less settled.

The relative strength of B008 (DMFT). Eriksson's opening first choice drew little support, and Kroll, Lindroth and Mehlig question whether a method prize can be anchored to one discovery. Eriksson himself notes limited accuracy for nonlocal correlations.
attribution_disputes: B012 (Katori, Ye): Takamoto, Hong, Ludlow, Lemke and the NIST, PTB and SYRTE groups, and the strontium versus ytterbium first-demonstration history, are not covered by the two names. Lindroth and Kroll state they cannot verify the first-demonstration history, and Johansson and Mehlig say the same. Members differ on whether this can be handled in the citation text (Olsson, Kroll) or may make a two-name prize unfair (Danielsson).

B042 (MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero, Bistritzer): Olsson doubts the inclusion of Bistritzer, and Pearce now concedes the attribution is less settled than he had assumed. Members cite Cao, Dean, Young, Efetov, Kim-type groups and earlier band-flattening theorists (Lopes dos Santos and others) as missing from the three names. Eriksson, Danielsson, Lindroth, Johansson, Kroll and Mehlig raise the divided experimental credit. This is the main attribution objection to B042.

B030 (Kane, Mele, Molenkamp): Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang (BHZ prediction tested by HgTe, with Zhang deceased) and the three-dimensional topological-insulator work are missing. Eriksson thinks a citation naming the first HgTe observation makes the trio defensible. Kroll, Olsson and Mehlig regard the gap as more serious than B012's.

B028 (Della Negra, Jenni, Virdee): three founding spokespersons or project leaders stand in for two collaborations of thousands, with analysis teams and accelerator builders absent. Danielsson (the opening first-place proponent) acknowledges the problem, and Johansson, Mehlig and Pearce say it keeps B028 below B012. Mehlig would accept it only if a principled attribution rule can be stated.

B005 and B008: Girvin and Huang are absent from the circuit QED names (Johansson, Lindroth, Olsson, Danielsson); Metzner, Müller-Hartmann, Jarrell and Rozenberg are absent from the DMFT names (Eriksson, Lindroth, Mehlig, Danielsson).
maturity_disputes: Whether the redefinition of the SI second must come before a lattice-clock prize. Eriksson treats the impact as unfinished. Danielsson, Johansson, Kroll, Olsson and Pearce say the measurement results already exist and a prize need not wait on an external metrological process.

Whether B042 is mature enough about eight years after the 2018 experiments. Johansson, Lindroth, Kroll, Mehlig, Olsson, Danielsson and Eriksson cite the unsettled superconducting mechanism, sample dependence and the open credit. Lindroth would let it mature one or two more years. Kroll and Eriksson say they could support it as lead, or Eriksson would put it first, if the committee judges the field's growth to outweigh its youth.

Whether the 2025 superconducting-circuit prize makes B005 look repetitive so soon (Eriksson, Lindroth, Mehlig, Kroll, Danielsson, Pearce). Kroll adds that the 2012 prizes did not block the 2025 award, so the risk is symmetric.

Whether the 2016 topological-phases prize reduces the novelty of B030 (Eriksson raises it himself), and whether the 2005 and 2012 prizes leave enough room for a further precision-measurement award (Johansson, Kroll, Olsson).
B002 (quantum error correction) rests on experiments that are still early, according to Johansson and Mehlig, and was not preferred by anyone.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Johansson (B005 and other superconducting-circuit and quantum-computing candidates): directs WACQT at Chalmers, works on circuit and waveguide QED, and has documented links to Per Delsing, C. M. Wilson and Anton Frisk Kockum. He does not propose B005 as preferred or alternative. He also records no specific conflict for B012, B030 or B042.

Eriksson (B008, DMFT): DMFT and LDA+DMFT methods are on his Uppsala profile and he ranked B008 first in the opening, so he should be cautious in advocating it or consider recusing from any final vote on it. He records no link to B012, B030 or B042.

Kroll (B005, and more loosely B020 and B002): WACQT involvement is flagged as a possible recusal issue, and he would not push those as preferred. For B012 he notes his stay in John Hall's laboratory is in the same broad laser-metrology milieu as JILA, with no documented tie to Katori or Ye.

Lindroth (disclosure only): documented collaboration with Anne L'Huillier, the Lund attosecond group and Ursula Keller's ETH Zurich group. Wallraff of B005 is at ETH Zurich, but no relationship with him is documented. She makes no other connection claim.

Olsson (B012, record only): long exchanges with Japanese universities including a University of Tokyo fellowship, and Katori is at the University of Tokyo and RIKEN, but no co-authorship or direct collaboration is documented.
Danielsson and Mehlig record no specific conflict. Pearce, as Chair, records none and says he will not favour any field.
questions_for_round2: Can the committee confirm the first-demonstration and credit history of lattice clocks (Takamoto, Hong, Ludlow, Lemke, Yb and Sr groups, and NIST, PTB, SYRTE), and if so, is a Katori and Ye pairing still fair, or can the omissions be handled in the citation text?

What citation wording makes the magic-wavelength lattice with many-atom interrogation plainly distinct from the 2005 frequency-comb and 2012 single-ion control prizes, and does Eriksson accept that wording as resolving his novelty concern?

Is a pending redefinition of the SI second a maturity condition for B012, or is the demonstrated and reproduced 10^-18 performance sufficient? Eriksson is the only member who treats it as leaving the impact unfinished.

Eriksson, what specifically keeps B030 above B012 for you beyond preference for a conceptual discovery, and could you support B012 as lead with B030 retained as a later candidate? Conversely, can Kane, Mele and Molenkamp with a citation naming the HgTe observation be worded fairly to Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang and the 3D work, or is the BHZ omission disqualifying, as Kroll, Olsson and Mehlig imply?

For B042, what would make the maturity and attribution concerns resolvable, for example a settled account of the superconducting mechanism, and is the Bistritzer inclusion and the Cao, Dean, Young and Efetov credit question settleable within a three-name limit? Would the supporters of B012 accept B042 as lead if those points were resolved?
After the 2025 prize, does any member now argue that B005 or B020 should be a preferred part this year, and if not, should they be recorded as later-year candidates?
Is a second prize part required at all, and if one were added, could any single-name or two-name part from the alternatives (B030, B042, B020) be allocated fairly under the three-person cap?
summary.chair_observation: Seven of eight members explicitly prefer B012 as a single prize part with Katori and Ye, and all seven agree its attribution is the cleanest on the shortlist. The one dissent is Eriksson, who prefers B030 and lists B012 and B042 as alternatives. Several members changed their first choice between the opening and round 1, with Danielsson, Johansson and Pearce moving to B012, so opening ranks and round-1 preferences should be kept apart. The remaining disagreement concerns the novelty of B012 relative to the 2005 and 2012 prizes, whether to wait for the redefinition of the second, whether B042 or B030 is a sounder choice despite their credit and maturity gaps, and how to word a citation that is honest about lattice-clock credit beyond the two names. Round 2 should decide whether those points can be settled in citation wording rather than in the laureate list.
